subject: IslandBridge private deployment: secure onramp & networking orchestration
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@islandbridge.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@islandbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood private topology + next steps for onramp

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Friday. As we discussed, IslandBridge is proceeding with the Private deployment option — we'd like to lock the initial networking topology and confirm the cadence for the handoff to engineering.

High-level asks from our side: 
- Verify VPC peering options (transit gateway vs. VPC peering).
- Private endpoints (ALB/NLB) and whether Redwood will provide signed certs or we bring our own.
- On-prem package requirements for our appliance team (OS, ports, certs, disk).
- A short checklist we can give to infra to avoid back-and-forth.

Attached is a rough network diagram and our internal security intake. Can you please propose a 2-week orchestration plan and identify any blockers?

Best,
Daniel
Senior Infrastructure Lead
IslandBridge

Attachments: islandbridge_network_diagram_v1.pdf, islandbridge_security_intake.xlsx

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@islandbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood private topology + next steps for onramp

Hi Daniel — great to hear IslandBridge is moving forward. Looping in Monica (implementation lead) and Grace (network SME) to own the technical handoff.

Quick response to your bullets:
- VPC peering: our standard recommendation for the first phase is VPC peering for smaller accounts because it minimizes cross-account routing complexity; for multi-VPC environments we can switch to Transit Gateway during stage 2. Will flag this in the runbook.
- Private endpoints: we support both customer-managed certs (recommended) and Redwood-managed certs for short-lived proofs. We'll outline both flows.
- On-prem package: Monica will send an appliance manifest (OS, ports, service accounts, HSM/KMS notes).
- Checklist: see attached from our side — it's a condensed onboarding checklist we hand to infra teams.

Proposed orchestration plan (high level):
1) Week 0: Kickoff + network snapshot and firewall rule signoff (1 call).
2) Week 1: VPC peering setup + private endpoint validation in staging.
3) Week 2: On-prem appliance install (if applicable) + end-to-end smoke tests.
4) Week 3: Cutover window + rollback plan.

Monica — can you propose specific dates for the above and add required PR/ACL entries?

Thanks,
Aditya
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_onprem-checklist.xlsx

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@islandbridge.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood private topology + next steps for onramp

Hi all — thanks Aditya. Added Laura (delivery manager) for scheduling and runbook signoff. Below is the more detailed implementation checklist and a note on known compatibility items. I attached a formal SOW draft (v2) for legal matching.

Implementation checklist (deliverable-driven):
- Pre-kickoff (deliverable): Customer to provide VPC CIDR ranges, current NAT/firewall rules, and peering admin contact. (Owners: IslandBridge)
- Kickoff (call): 60 minutes, agenda: roles, timeline, emergency contacts, testing windows. (Owner: Redwood PM)
- Network prep (task): Create peering connection, exchange route tables, and add specific CIDR allow-lists for 10.10.0.0/16 and 172.20.0.0/16. Confirm MTU and TCP MSS settings if using transit. (Owner: IslandBridge + Redwood network)
- Private endpoint (task): Provision internal NLB in customer VPC; validate DNS injection via Route53 private zone or customer DNS. If customer uses on-prem DNS, we'll provide SRV/A records to import. (Owner: IslandBridge)
- Certificates (decision point): If IslandBridge will manage certs, we will provide CSR template and expected SANs. If Redwood manages, we will coordinate ACME + preflight validation. (Owner: InfoSec + IslandBridge)
- On-prem package (deliverable): Appliance tarball (.tar.gz) with install script, systemd unit, and a docs folder. Minimums: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM, 200GB disk, ports 443, 22 (ssh restricted), 2379 (if etcd used). HSM/KMS integration notes included for customers requiring FIPS. (Owner: Redwood eng)
- Staging validation (task): Smoke tests including model inference loop, KV cache persistence, and latency SLO sampling. (Owner: Redwood + IslandBridge SRE)
- Cutover (task): 2-hour maintenance window with pre- and post-check snaps and rollback playbook. (Owner: Delivery + IslandBridge infra)

Compatibility notes:
- If IslandBridge is behind a corporate proxy that does TLS interception, we need a proxy-friendly package and explicit exception list for the KV endpoints.
- We recommend enabling prefix cache for predictable throughput; we'll provide load profiles.

Proposed dates (local PST):
- Kickoff: Tues 2026-11-23 10:00–11:00 (tentative)
- VPC peering + staging validation: 2026-11-24–26
- On-prem install window: 2026-11-30–12/02

Daniel/Priya — please confirm kickoff and the CIDR blocks by EOD 11/20 so we can lock resources.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_IslandBridge_v2.docx, redwood_onprem-install-manifest.txt

From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@islandbridge.com>

Thanks Monica — that checklist looks good and the timeline is reasonable. Confirming kickoff Tue 2026-11-23 at 10:00 PST. CIDR ranges below: 10.10.0.0/16 (apps), 172.20.0.0/16 (db), 192.168.200.0/24 (on-prem interconnect).

A couple quick questions before kickoff:
- Do you have a template for the CSR and expected SAN list?
- For the on-prem appliance, do you provide a preseeded image or only an installer script? Our appliance team prefers images.

I'll upload the network ACLs and a short inventory this afternoon to the Confluence page. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Priya Rao
